summary:
PASS WITH CONDITIONS (round 2). Both round-1 highs are fixed: reconstruction now answers state across transitions/moves with creation seeding (audit.ts:327-438) and the real system-transition executor + customer reopen are integration-tested (system-transition-real-executor.test.ts).
R3/R4/R5/R8/R9/R11/R12 fixed; R6 and R10 partial; R7 carried to P3. Cursor fix in listSubmissions/listOwnSubmissions is correct (consistent ms truncation in predicate and ORDER BY) but bypasses the created_at indexes.
New mediums: S1 every successful customer reopen leaves a false 'Reopen needs review' flag; S2 system hops take the first matching edge, so a gated edge on the same pair can be skipped depending on order.
Security pass: SLA/submission recipients staff/requester-scoped and reach-checked, portal SLA {state,dueAt} only, audit routes reach-gated, customers refused; no high issues.
Conditions: C1 browser-verify SLA panel, History disclosure, reopen badge, portal SLA (AGENTS.md:48); C2 fix S1; C3 fix or explicitly accept S2 with a test.
Requirements: 117 met, 15 partial, 5 blocked, 0 not_met; remaining partial/blocked are non-core or carried (P3/P4/P5/owner hold).

findings.problem: The R6 fix writes reopen_requested {reason:'pending'} in the reply transaction for every reply to a resolved item. On success requestCustomerReopen returns at :94 without superseding that row, and on refusal it adds a second reopen_requested row. The web renders every reopen_requested row (regardless of payload.reason) as the warning badge 'Reopen needs review - could not be reopened automatically'.
findings.impact: Every successful customer reopen leaves a false 'needs review' flag next to the system transition; refused reopens show two flags. Staff learn to ignore the flag that WF-21 relies on.
findings.recommended_fix: Use a distinct verb (e.g. reopen_received) for the durable in-tx record and render the warning only for reopen_requested rows whose reason is non-pending, or mark the pending row resolved/superseded on success. Add an integration test through postSubmissionMessage (customer reply on a resolved item) asserting exactly one transitioned row and no warning row on success.

findings.problem: For a system actor every role-gated edge is legal (:313-314) and the scheduled hop takes the FIRST offerable edge for the template pair (:370-374). Version validation only forbids duplicates of (from,to,role) (workflow.ts:623), so a version can hold two edges for the same pair (different roles, or a null-from 'any' edge plus a specific one), one ungated and one requiring approval or carrying guards; which gate/guards apply to the hop depends on array order.
findings.impact: Whether a scheduled hop is refused by an approval gate or guard is order-dependent (non-deterministic across republishes); no test covers a guarded or multi-edge pair. Not a privilege escalation: both edges are admin-authored and the ungated one is a path some role can already take.
findings.recommended_fix: For system hops, refuse (blocked) when any matching edge in the type-filtered offerable set requires approval/CAB, and evaluate guards of all matching edges (most restrictive wins). Add integration tests for a two-edge pair and a guarded (children_closed) pair.

findings.problem: AGENTS.md:48 requires every touched screen to be compared against Kaneo 42bb8011 in a browser. Only Workflows list/detail and the triage queue have screenshots (docs/report/screens/p2-*.jpg). The SLA panel (hand-positioned absolute span marker with inline style left:% at :148-166, calendar line, pause line), History disclosure + reconstruction table, reopen warning badge and portal SLA badge have never been rendered in a browser.
findings.impact: Visual/UX regressions on the work-item detail and portal would be unobserved; under AGENTS.md this is a phase condition.
findings.recommended_fix: Seed an item with an SLA policy on a named calendar, an open waiting_customer pause and an at_risk metric; capture the detail SLA panel, History disclosure with 'state then' table, a reopen flag row, and the portal submission with SLA badge; compare to Kaneo and file screenshots in docs/report/screens.

findings.problem: WF-21 tests call requestCustomerReopen directly; the reply transaction's durable write (intake/repository.ts:2339-2345) and post-commit sequencing are never executed by a test.
findings.impact: The S1 false flag and any regression in the in-tx durability are not caught.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a test that posts a customer reply on a resolved item via postSubmissionMessage and asserts activity rows and final state.

findings.problem: 'assignee=claimed' has no server parameter and is filtered on the loaded page only; an unresolved request-type id also falls back to page-local filtering.
findings.impact: A shared ?assignee=claimed queue URL can show different/incomplete rows than the server total.
findings.recommended_fix: Accept assignee=claimed server-side (claimed_by IS NOT NULL) and resolve unknown type ids to a 400/empty result instead of page-local filtering.

findings.problem: The cursor fix orders and compares on date_trunc('milliseconds', created_at), which cannot use submission_state_created_idx / submission_requester_created_idx (0096:163-164); every page sorts the full filtered set. The fix itself is correct (consistent truncation on both predicate and ORDER BY, id tie-break).
findings.impact: Queue/portal pagination degrades linearly with backlog size.
findings.recommended_fix: Keep raw created_at ordering and carry full precision in the cursor (select created_at::text or extract(epoch) with microseconds), or add an expression index on (date_trunc('milliseconds', created_at), id).

findings.problem: Sibling cursor with the same precision class, pre-existing (not in the P2 diff): candidate-page loops (bulk mark-read/delete and list) set the cursor from the driver's millisecond Date and compare raw microsecond created_at (defaultNow, schema.ts:1399) in DESC order, so rows at the page boundary sharing the millisecond (including all rows of one fan-out tx, which share now()) are SKIPPED, not repeated. pending-action cursor (pending-action/service.ts:187,393) is safe because created_at is app-set in ms; activity feed already truncates (list-work-item-activity.ts:91-106).
findings.impact: Rare: bulk mark-all-read/delete-all or the inbox list can leave/miss rows when >100 candidates and a tie straddles the page boundary.
findings.recommended_fix: Apply the same date_trunc (or full-precision cursor) to inbox cursorPredicate and order; audit remaining keyset cursors.

findings.problem: Headers still say 'WRITTEN, NOT YET RUN' though the coordinator reports them green; the R4 test calls transitionWorkItem with null identity and no system request (not a production call shape); the AU-9 test hand-writes the created and project-move activity rows instead of driving create/move controllers.
findings.impact: Misleading provenance; the move payload shape (move-work-item.ts:514-521) is asserted only by convention.
findings.recommended_fix: Update headers; drive R4 through a person transition; build the AU-9 move through moveWorkItem.

findings.problem: Doc comments contradict behaviour: scheduled-transition.ts says a refused/blocked hop stays pending and is retried (it is cancelled terminally); system-transition.ts says no executor is registered (transition-work-item.ts:1194 registers it); contract still says reminder-scan fires rows (R18).
findings.impact: Maintainers are misled about failure semantics.
findings.recommended_fix: Correct the comments and add a decision-log entry for the one-minute scheduled-transition job.

findings.problem: A hop whose execution throws (not a refusal) stays pending and is retried every minute forever; no attempt counter or backoff (known carry).
findings.impact: Log noise and a permanently degraded job for a poisoned row.
findings.recommended_fix: Add attempts/last_error columns and cancel with a flagged activity after N failures.

findings.problem: The auto-decline reason sent to the customer says 'You can reopen it at any time to continue' but no customer reopen route or portal action exists until P3.
findings.impact: A promise the product cannot keep in this phase.
findings.recommended_fix: Drop the reopen sentence until the P3 route ships, or ship the route.

findings.problem: The present-value baseline covers only stateId/assigneeId/priority/title; other fields set at creation and never changed (description, dates, type, parent) are absent, while the route description says untouched fields do not appear at all.
findings.impact: Inconsistent snapshot completeness; documentation does not match output.
findings.recommended_fix: Extend the baseline to the journalled field set (or seed from the created payload) and align the route description. Also: auditValueLabel falls through to truncate(value) for unrecognised fields (apps/web/src/lib/audit-history-format.ts:108), so a typeId/label change can still show a raw id or JSON despite the 'never a raw id' comment; map those fields too.

findings.problem: Portal SLA due instant uses toLocaleString() without timezone name (staff side uses formatSlaInstant with timeZoneName) and English defaults are duplicated in code (SLA_DEFAULT).
findings.impact: Minor inconsistency; English fallbacks bypass the catalogue.
findings.recommended_fix: Reuse formatSlaInstant/formatDate and rely on catalogue keys.

findings.problem: R14 unchanged: state template names come from projects[0]'s state-templates route.
findings.impact: Workspace with no projects (or no reach to projects[0]) shows unknown names in transitions and the validation dialog.
